The ticket's own acceptance criteria - 6 of 6 met
A setting to choose between Line-by-line and Total-rounded
Default is Line-by-line for all existing and new shops; nothing changes until it is switched
PASSED — 7 of 7 existing locations, 5 of 5 newly created ones, and 993 of 1,000 existing invoices untouched
Total-rounded shows the QuickBooks $0.01 open-balance warning
Applies going forward; does not rewrite already-issued invoices
PASSED — flipped in both directions with an invoice already issued
And the four open questions, as answered on 18 August
Two options, "Line by line (default)" and "Invoice total", each with a one-line explanation
location A billed 2.71 while untouched location B billed 2.70 on the same subtotal
Not-yet-invoiced follows the location's setting; issued invoices keep their billed rounding
Not single-rate — rounds once per rate
confirmed on two rates (GST+PST) and on three stacked rates
Locations dialog shows "Sales Tax Rounding" = "Line By Line (Default)" on an untouched location, no warning banner
The dropdown offers both options, each with its own explanation line
Picking "Invoice Total" raises the $0.01 QuickBooks warning banner
Switch back to the default — banner gone, save, reopen, persisted
A brand-new location saves as line-by-line without anyone touching the field (5 of 5)
Case 1, the real reported invoice INV-S-26020 — subtotal 6,055.65, tax 302.81 on the default
Case 2, 9.75% on 18.54 — 1.80 default / 1.81 invoice-total (rises a cent)
Case 3, 8% on 80.67 — 6.46 default / 6.45 invoice-total (drops a cent)
Case 5b, three stacked rates on 27.81 — 2.22 both ways
Case 5b per-rate breakdown — 1.11 / 0.84 / 0.27 default vs 1.11 / 0.83 / 0.28 invoice-total, both summing to 2.22
Half-cent lines on one rate, 3 x 9.27 at 9.75% — 2.70 / 2.71
Two tax rates (GST 5% + PST 7%), each rounded once on its own base; the two rate lines add up to the invoice tax
Shop supplies enabled — the supplies tax and the line taxes still add up exactly, no plus-or-minus a cent drift
Zero-tax location on "Invoice total" — tax 0.00 everywhere, no crash
Invoice issued on the default, then the location switched to "Invoice total" — invoice unchanged
Invoice issued on "Invoice total", then switched back — invoice unchanged
Full payment on an "Invoice total" invoice — balance exactly $0.00
Full payment on a default-setting invoice — balance exactly $0.00
Partial payment, $10.00 of $30.52 — balance $20.52, to the cent
The setting is per location: A on "Invoice total" billed 2.71 while B, untouched, billed 2.70 on the same subtotal
Invoice screen and the rendered invoice document agree figure for figure, both modes
Customer Invoice export reconciliation — case 1's 13 per-line tax amounts add up to exactly 302.81 on the default and exactly 302.78 on Invoice total
All 19 invoices this run produced reconcile in the export, per-line tax to invoice tax
All 7 existing locations read "Line by line (default)" without anyone setting them
All 1,000 existing invoices read individually — 993 still carry their own GST 5% snapshot; the only 7 that do not are the ones this run created
All 863 paid invoices still sit at a zero balance, no new one-cent residue
Return 1 of 3 received parts on an "Invoice total" invoice - the issued invoice is unchanged (244.00 / 23.79 / 267.79)
The same return on a "Line by line" invoice, run as a control - identical, also unchanged
Post the vendor credit for that returned part - the issued invoice is still unchanged

END TO END THROUGH THE UI: "Invoice total" chosen in the Locations dialog by clicking and saved with the Save button, then a work order invoiced - it bills 2.71, where the default bills 2.70 on the same three lines
Receiving is reachable from the UI and works: all 30 Receive links on Parts > Purchase Orders open the same receive screen, and clicking one received the part
Taxable fee or discount on a work order

NOT TESTABLE - both entry points reach the full dialog, but Add is disabled and the API refuses until a QuickBooks Fee/Discount item is mapped, and no QuickBooks company is attached to this org so that mapping cannot be created here
The QuickBooks side - the $0.01 open balance the banner warns about
NOT TESTABLE - needs a QuickBooks-connected company; a manual-tester task
Every figure below is on an

work order, so it is frozen - opening it tomorrow shows the same number. Each image carries its work-order number and the build marker in the header band, and every box is drawn from the real on-screen geometry of the value it points at. A work order that is not yet invoiced re-prices against its location's current setting, so it is not valid evidence.
1. The setting on an untouched location: "Line By Line (Default)", and no warning banner.
2. Picking "Invoice Total" raises the QuickBooks $0.01 open-balance warning (AC5). Saving and reopening keeps the value; switching back removes the banner and also persists.

3. CASE 1, the real reported invoice, on the DEFAULT — subtotal 6,055.65, tax $302.81, total $6,358.46. This is the number on the customer's paper invoice, so it is the proof the default path was not changed.
4. The same case on "Invoice total" — tax $302.78, total $6,358.43. Same 13 taxable lines, same subtotal; only the rounding method differs.
5. AC3 — the ticket's example 1 (8% on $80.67) on the default: tax $6.46.
6. AC4 — the same example on "Invoice total": tax $6.45, one cent DOWN.
7. AC3 — the ticket's example 2 (9.75% on $18.54) on the default: tax $1.80.

8. AC4 — the same example on "Invoice total": tax $1.81, one cent UP. Cases 2 and 3 together show the setting is not a one-way "tax goes down" lever — anyone checking only one of them will report the other as a bug.
9. Three stacked rates (4% + 3% + 1% on $27.81) on the default: 1.11 / 0.84 / 0.27.

10. The same on "Invoice total": 1.11 / 0.83 / 0.28. The 3% row drops a cent and the 1% row gains one, the rows still add up to the invoice tax, and the TOTAL is identical ($2.22) in both modes — so checking only the total would miss this entirely. This is the proof each rate is rounded once on its own base.
11. A full payment on an "Invoice total" invoice closes to exactly $0.00 — no one-cent residue on ShopView's own side.
12. Location A (Staging Heavy Duty) set to "Invoice total": tax $2.71.
13. Location B (Staging Lethbridge), left untouched on the default: tax $2.70 on the SAME tax model and the SAME $27.81 subtotal. The setting is per location, not per organisation.

14. An issued invoice from 12 February 2025. This run deliberately changed that location's whole tax model five times over; the invoice still reads its own frozen GST 5% / $141.66 / $2,974.79 with a zero balance. Note the caption: the Financial Info panel on the left RE-PRICES an old work order live, so it is not the billed figure — the issued invoice on the right is.
15. S-16001 - a vendor part received on this branch, then 1 of 3 returned. This is the setup for the two exhibits below.
16. S-15999, billed under "Invoice total" - the issued invoice document read AFTER returning one of the three parts: subtotal $244.00, tax $23.79, total $267.79, exactly what it was billed.
17. The same test run as a control on "Line by line" (S-16001) - identical result, so a part return does not rewrite an issued invoice under either rounding method (AC6).

18. The credit for a returned part (Parts > Returns > Receive Credit > Process Return). It is a VENDOR credit: priced at the part's $10.00 cost rather than its $80.00 sell price, with Tax pre-filled at 5% of that cost from the workplace rate - not this location's 9.75% sales-tax model. It read identically under both rounding modes, so this setting does not reach it.

19. Add Part Fee / Discount on S-16003, showing the full dialog including the Taxable control, and Add Fee disabled behind the QuickBooks mapping banner. The work-order kebab route behaves identically.

20. THE END-USER PATH: "Invoice total" was chosen in the Locations dialog by clicking and saved with the Save button, then S-16006 was invoiced - it bills tax $2.71. The same three lines under the default bill $2.70, so the setting a user saves on the screen is demonstrably the one that reaches the invoice.

21. Where a user lands after clicking Receive on Parts > Purchase Orders. All 30 Receive links on that list open this screen, the part row on a work order leads here too, and both save through the same call. Parts > Vendor Invoices rows open a read-only view with no receive action.
Three things worth folding into the QA handoff
The accepted wire value for the setting is
returns 400 "Invalid sales tax rounding method." The UI and the handoff both call the option "Invoice total", so automation has to discover this.
is a live re-price of the work order, not the issued invoice. For the February-2025 invoice S-4802 it returned today's date, the location's current tax model and a different subtotal, while
returned the real frozen invoice. Anyone checking "did the invoice move?" against details will report a false alarm.

ignores the workplace_id in the payload and uses the session's active location. If they differ, the work order picks up the wrong location's tax and - because canned lines are location-scoped - the canned-line dropdown returns "No results" and lines fail to save with no error shown.

- both entry points behave identically: the work-order kebab (Add Work Order Fee / Discount) and the part row's kebab (Add Part Fee / Discount). Both open the dialog and its live preview computes; both leave
answers 409 "Connect a QuickBooks item for fees before adding a fee." Front end and back end enforce the same guard, so it is not a front-end-only gate.
Worth a look: the mapping-status flag disagrees with the rest of the state.

returns an Intuit OAuth URL still waiting to be used, and the admin page offers only a Connect button. Three signals say no QuickBooks company is attached, which means the Fee/Discount item mapping cannot be created from inside ShopView at all. Ruled out as bypasses: an adjustment template (creates fine, 201, still blocked), passing templateId on the add call, the line-level labour adjustment button, and

Every one of the 30 Receive links on Parts > Purchase Orders points at

One question rather than a finding

: the handoff asks that a credit against an "Invoice total" invoice pro-rate its credited tax from the frozen invoice tax. The build instead charges the workplace purchase rate on the part's cost, and the ticket itself says nothing about credits - so
is the vendor credit meant to carry the workplace purchase tax as built, or the customer's frozen sales tax as the handoff reads?

: customer Aaborough Works (contact Jeffrey Burns), asset 2020 Ford Transit VIN 86J8FAC1VALJ43SJY, locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, labour type "ZZ8815 Unit" at $1.00/hour so a line can be dialled to the cent, and tax models created for the run: ZZ8815 8pct, ZZ8815 9.75pct, ZZ8815 Stacked (4%+3%+1%), ZZ8815 GSTPST (5%+7%). The part-return work orders are S-15999
. Every exhibit's work order is named in its header band so any figure here can be re-opened and re-read.
Driven through the UI, and driven by API - stated plainly
because an end user works on the screen.
The feature under test was exercised on the screen:

the Locations dialog was opened, both options read from the dropdown, "Invoice total" chosen by clicking, the QuickBooks banner observed, saved with the Save button, and the saved value confirmed to survive a reopen and a hard reload - and check 34 then carried that UI-saved setting through to an invoice, which billed 2.71 rather than the default's 2.70. Receiving and the vendor credit were also driven by clicking.
What was driven by API is the scaffolding and the repetition:

creating each work order and its lines, completing it, raising the invoice, taking payments, and flipping the setting between the many pinned calculation cases. That is a deliberate speed trade-off on a 35-check run, and it is safe here because the tax is computed server-side and every figure quoted above was read back off the screen or the issued invoice document rather than from the call that created it. Worth knowing rather than assuming, so it is stated.
: the marker above was read at the start of the run, at the end, and again before this comment - unchanged each time, so every verdict here belongs to one build.
